note: One complete parent→child transition in the Darwin Gödel Machine: the outer driver samples a parent from the archive by a score-weighted lottery with an exploration bonus, the o1 diagnoser studies the parent's failures and proposes a fix, the parent coding agent rewrites its own code inside a Docker sandbox, and the child must survive a staged SWE-bench gauntlet plus a compile gate to join the archive. Two nested loops — a fixed evolutionary driver outside, an evolving two-tool coding agent inside.

steps.narrative: Each generation begins in DGM_outer.py: choose_selfimproves builds a candidate table from every archived child's metadata.json and samples parents with the default score_child_prop strategy — a sigmoid on score multiplied by 1/(1+children), so high-scoring nodes are favored but under-exploited branches keep an exploration bonus. It also picks what to fix: a pseudo-entry like solve_empty_patches some of the time, otherwise a uniformly random unresolved benchmark instance (a parent that resolved everything is skipped).
steps.representation:
archive = ['initial', 'a1…', 'b2…']       # every child dir is a member
weight(n) = sigmoid(10 * (score(n) - 0.5))  # winners preferred
          * 1 / (1 + children(n))            # exploration bonus for the idle
parent    = random.choices(archive, weight)  # with replacement
entry     = 'solve_empty_patches' | random unresolved instance id
steps.title: Sample a parent from the archive

steps.narrative: diagnose_problem sends the fixed o1-2024-12-17 diagnoser a system prompt containing the full current source of the coding agent — coding_agent.py, all of tools/, all of utils/, plus the ancestor patch files — explicitly excluding evo_utils.py, docker_utils.py, swe_log_parsers.py and the prompt module itself; DGM_outer.py and self_improve_step.py are never shown at all. The user prompt carries the failure evidence: the parent's logs, the unresolved entry — and the private SWE-bench test patch.
steps.representation:
diagnoser = o1-2024-12-17                 # fixed model, never evolved
system    = <coding_agent.py, tools/, utils/, ancestor diffs>
            # NEVER shown: DGM_outer.py, self_improve_step.py
user      = <parent logs, unresolved instance, PRIVATE test patch>
diagnose_problem(system, user) -> JSON      # the 'propose' half
steps.title: The diagnoser studies the parent

steps.narrative: o1 must answer with a strict JSON contract — log_summarization, potential_improvements, improvement_proposal, implementation_suggestion, problem_description — extracted with extract_json_between_markers and up to 3 retries on malformed output. The implementation_suggestion and problem_description are the real payload: they become the rewrite prompt handed to the parent agent. A later post-hoc impact score (−2..2) is stored in metadata but gates nothing.
steps.representation:
{
  "log_summarization":       ...,
  "potential_improvements":   ...,
  "improvement_proposal":    ...,
  "implementation_suggestion": ...,  # what to code
  "problem_description":     ...     # the rewrite prompt's core
}
extract_json_between_markers     # up to 3 retries
steps.title: o1 proposes the improvement

steps.narrative: The rewrite is the Gödel half: a fresh Docker container is built per attempt, the parent is materialized by applying every ancestor patch from initial in order with patch -p1, and a throwaway commit isolates the diff. Then a fresh instance of the parent coding agent itself runs inside the container against /dgm — coding_agent.py --problem_statement ... --git_dir /dgm/ --self_improve, 30-minute timeout — editing the live codebase with its bash and editor tools. Afterwards model_patch.diff is extracted and copied to the host: that diff against its parent is the child's entire genome.
steps.representation:
dgm-container-<run_id>                    # fresh sandbox
patch -p1 < initial..parent diffs         # materialize the parent
git add --all && git commit                # throwaway 'nonsense' commit
coding_agent.py --problem_statement "<proposal>"
                --git_dir /dgm/ --self_improve   # the PARENT rewrites itself
timeout 1800
model_patch.diff -> output_dgm/<run_id>/<child_id>/   # child born
steps.title: The parent rewrites itself — a child is born

steps.narrative: run_harness_swe evaluates the child in two stages: first the small subset (10 SWE-bench instances) with up to 5 parallel workers, scored by the official make_report and aggregated to overall_performance. Only if at least 4 of 10 instances resolve (test_more_threshold = 0.4) does the child graduate to the medium subset (50 instances), whose results overwrite the stage-1 score. The big subset (140) is never touched during evolution.
steps.representation:
stage 1: 10 instances, 5 workers      # cheap filter
  resolved/total -> overall_performance
stage 2: only if resolved >= 10 * 0.4  # >= 4 of 10
  50 instances -> OVERWRITES the score
stage 3: does not exist in the loop    # big subset is manual, post-hoc
steps.title: The child runs the benchmark gauntlet

steps.narrative: The compile gate — is_compiled_self_improve, then filter_compiled in the outer loop — admits a child only if its metadata has all four performance keys, it produced at least one non-empty patch, and it submitted the expected number of instances, which catches evals that crashed partway. Children that fail the gate keep their directories, logs, and patches on disk; they are simply never added to the archive.
steps.representation:
admit iff:
  metadata has all 4 performance keys
  AND resolved + unresolved > 0    # at least one non-empty patch
  AND total_submitted meets quota  # eval didn't crash partway
failed children stay on disk        # but never join the archive
steps.title: The compile gate decides admission

steps.narrative: update_archive appends the survivors under the default keep_all policy — every compiled child joins, even one that scores worse than its parent, which is what keeps the tree open-ended instead of greedy hill-climbing. Each generation appends one JSON line to dgm_metadata.jsonl recording the full archive list; each child dir carries metadata.json (run_id, parent_commit, entry, overall_performance), model_patch.diff, self_evo.md, self_improve.log, and predictions/.
steps.title: Archive updated, lineage recorded

steps.narrative: The loop repeats for up to 80 generations, two children per generation in a ThreadPoolExecutor with a 1.5-hour timeout per future — a bad child is logged, never fatal. The newborn re-enters the parent lottery immediately with children_count 0, i.e. the maximal exploration bonus, so a weak-but-fresh lineage can still win the next draw. Lineage is always reconstructible: walk the parent_commit chain back to initial and apply the patches oldest-first.
steps.representation:
for generation in range(max_generation=80):
    2 children, ThreadPoolExecutor, 1.5 h timeout each
    newborn: children_count = 0       # maximal exploration bonus
    weight = sigmoid(10*(score-0.5)) * 1/(1+children)
# a weak-but-fresh lineage can still win the next lottery
reconstruct = parent_commit chain -> patch -p1 oldest-first
steps.title: The next generation samples — possibly the newborn

title: One generation through the Darwin Gödel Machine
